lesson.title: Counting → Whole → Integers
lesson.html: Counting numbers: 1, 2, 3… Whole numbers add zero. Integers add the opposites: …−3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3…

lesson.title: Absolute value
lesson.html: The distance from zero on a number line. Distance is never negative: |−7| = 7.

lesson.title: Adding & subtracting
lesson.html:
Add a negative = combining with an absence.
Subtract a negative = taking away an absence (it's the same as adding the opposite).

lesson.title: Signs in multiplying & dividing
lesson.html:
Same signs → positive.
Different signs → negative.
Multiplying negatives = combining the opposite of a number of equal groups.

list.q: Why can positive and negative numbers be “equal opposites”?
list.a: They have the same absolute value but sit on opposite sides of zero
w: They both have the same sign
They are both greater than zero
list.why: Equal distance from zero, opposite directions.
Positive numbers are the ones that are not negative and negative numbers are the ones that are not positive — zero is its own number: neither.
Integers are the only set that includes negatives.
Add a negative: combining with an absence.
Subtract a negative: taking away an absence — which makes the value go UP.
Subtracting a negative = adding its opposite.
